title: Deep Dive I: Two Ramps and a Lever
blurb: The README's (a > 4) ? 10 : 12, worked by hand on one growing machine at a backlit workbench. A bend of copper becomes a ReLU ramp; two ramps and a lever make a bit; both belts always run and each shutter scales the tile it passes; infinity on the closed belt still poisons the tray. Four and a half gives five and six, fused into eleven; past two to the twenty-fourth a whole number gives twenty minus twelve, eight. Just below that edge, the odd number on the plate snaps a score to a bit in one instruction. What exact means, and why doubles broke things. Then the real library demands a promise about its input, shrinks the comparison to two operations, and gives eleven again when the promise is false: declarations are promises, not proofs. Promise only a range and a lens train magnifies by two to the hundred and forty-ninth. Sixteen against two, and a silent plant for later.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: both branches run (machine 2). Cut on motion: the camera rises behind the ramps as they stand in silhouette against the window bay, revealing two black conveyor belts that never stop, one carrying '10' tiles and the other '12' tiles, each running toward a single output tray through its own paper shutter. On 'Both' the belts come up to speed (beat belts). On 'bit' a thin rod from the lever of s03 runs to both shutters: as the marble sits at 5, the lever reads 1 and the 10 shutter swings fully open while the 12 shutter closes fully. The shutters SCALE what they pass (the rule for the whole dive): a fully open shutter lets a 10 through unchanged; a shut shutter squeezes each 12 flat and re-letters it 0 as it passes, and the 0 tiles slide harmlessly into the tray beside the 10 (beat shutters). The formula appears on the clipped card. On 'other' the marble rolls to 3: the lever reads 0 and the shutters swap with a single clack; now the 10s come through as 0 and a whole 12 drops into the tray (beat swap). Hold: the belts keep running, both of them, the whole time.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: what the runtime really builds (Tags on Wires, machine 5). Crossfade back to the backlit workbench, the window bay warm, haze at board height. The input a is drawn as a single copper wire running into the machine. On 'compare' a monospace label chip clips to the comparison and the machine's lever locks with a small red stop: no range, no comparison (beat refuse). On 'range' the narrator's hands tie a small card to the wire of a giving its range (beat rangeTag). On 'Promise' the hands reach up to the copper line, untie tag 6 (the README's (a > 4) ? 10 : 12 with its small print 'For an integer a') and carry it down (beat retie); on 'whole' they re-tie it onto the wire of a and the tag's small print re-letters itself in ink as 'grid 1', lettering on the tag itself (beat reletter). On 'number' the two ramps and lever fold together into a smaller rig of two little boards in series, with its two formulas on the clipped card (beat shrink); a brass operation counter on the post ticks down and stops at 2. In the hold the marble checks three whole numbers on the existing number line (beat checks): at 5 the first board reads 0 and the second 1, and a 10 tile drops; at 4 they read 1 and 0, a 12; at 3 they read 2 and nought (the ramp cannot go below zero), a 12. shots.visual: THIS SHOT: no grid, only a range: the sign-cascade lens train (machine 3; one of the film's five images). Cut on motion: the camera follows the wire of a along the bench to its far end, where the lamp is lowered nearly to dark and only the lenses glow. From the left a hairline of copper light, the difference a minus four, so thin it is barely visible, enters a train of six backlit paper lenses mounted on black card stands. On 'gap' the hairline is shown flickering at the edge of visibility (beat hairline). On 'magnifies' it passes the first lens, marked ×2^14, and thickens; each of the next five lenses, marked ×2^24, follows at one lens per beat of the score, each followed by a stop that clips the beam at height 1 (beat lenses); a brass magnification dial winds to 2^149. On 'faintest' the beam reaches the seventh stage, the final ReGLU (×2^15 inside a ramp), then a flip, and floods the frame's right side as a solid copper bar (beat bar). On 'sixteen-operation' an operation counter settles at 16 ops in 15 layers, counting the comparison bit alone, and the bit reads 1 (beat sixteen); on 'ten' the bit drives the select: the bar opens the 10 shutter fully and a 10 tile drops (beat ten). Hold on the full bar.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the lesson. crossfade to a parchment plate: the lens train (left, long) and the two-board rig (right, small) drawn side by side in ink at the same scale, the lens train running nearly the width of the plate. On 'Sixteen' each rig's operation count inks beneath it (beat compare). On 'sentence' the 'grid 1' tag on the small rig's wire glows copper (beat honest); on 'fourteen' fourteen of the lens train's sixteen operation marks fade out one by one, leaving two, matching the small rig (beat fourteen). In the hold, the narrator's hands untie tag 6 from the wire and carry it back up to the copper line, where it hangs again, its small print 'For an integer a' showing, a slack thread over the Lifespan Rule. TAG-LINE STAGING (meta staging.tagLine): WORKSHOP AT THE BENCH: tag 6 is lifted from the line onto the bench's plates and back; the line sits higher in frame (66%), cropped by the plates below.
